items.author: Abby Sunderland

items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: One day that same year, I told my dad that someday, I would sail around the world alone.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: Fewer people have successfully solo-circumnavigated the globe than have journeyed into space.

items.sourceLine: Fewer people have successfully solo-circumnavigated the globe than have journeyed into space.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: All the ingenuity, all the high-tech gear, all the jury-rigging—sometimes the sea would rip it all away until there was only you, the Creator, and His mercy.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: I wanted to break the record, of course, and become the youngest person to sail around the world solo and unassisted.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: I wanted to break the record, of course, and become the youngest person to sail around the world solo and unassisted.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: On October 19, 2009, my sixteenth birthday, Wild Eyes officially became mine! Now it was really happening.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: On October 19, 2009, my sixteenth birthday, Wild Eyes officially became mine! Now it was really happening.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: The critics barged in to harp on every decision we made...Sadly, I began to doubt myself. Maybe I was too young. Maybe I wasn’t a good enough sailor.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: The critics barged in to harp on every decision we made. . .Sadly, I began to doubt myself. Maybe I was too young. Maybe I wasn’t a good enough sailor.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: After the week of stormy weather, she set sail under sunny skies, on a glassy sea with a big swell running.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: After the week of stormy weather, she set sail under sunny skies, on a glassy sea with a big swell running.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: I was so thankful that my parents trusted me enough and had enough faith in my abilities to let me follow my passion and try to do something great, even if I might fail.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: I was so thankful that my parents trusted me enough and had enough faith in my abilities to let me follow my passion and try to do something great, even if I might fail.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: I saw the loose tiller jolt hard to the side as the boat began to spin.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: I saw the loose tiller jolt hard to the side as the boat began to spin.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: When a sailor overcomes crushing adversity, there’s a massive sense of accomplishment.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: When a sailor overcomes crushing adversity, there’s a massive sense of accomplishment.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: If a big wave came at the wrong moment, it would sweep me off into forty-eight-degree water, where I might last twenty minutes. Drowning quickly might be better.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: If a big wave came at the wrong moment, it would sweep me off into forty-eight-degree water, where I might last twenty minutes. Drowning quickly might be better.

items.author: Abby Sunderland

items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: Slowly, my brain let me in on the fact that I had just come this close to dying.

items.author: Abby Sunderland

items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: Going up the mast is one of the most dangerous things you can do as a solo sailor.

items.author: Abby Sunderland

items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: The terrifying physics of going up-mast in heavy seas are inescapable.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: Even without looking I knew: there was no way I still had a mast. And without a mast, the trip was over.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: Even without looking I knew: there was no way I still had a mast. And without a mast, the trip was over.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: Fifty feet of mast lay in the heaving water, downed lines and shrouds holding it there.
items.section: Unsinkable: A Young Woman's Courageous Battle on the High Seas (2011)
items.sourceLine: Fifty feet of mast lay in the heaving water, downed lines and shrouds holding it there.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: I knew that even if I was able to call for help, I was in a place so remote that it wasn’t likely there would be anyone who could help me. And even if there were, it could take weeks.

items.author: Abby Sunderland
items.quote: In that moment it dawned on me that everything has to line up perfectly for something to turn out this awful.

items.author: Abby Sunderland

items.quote: I had previously announced that I am above trends and leanings, above party politics and political parties. This is because I strive for the people as a whole to serve them.

items.author: Abd al-Karim Qasim
items.quote: Brothers! The days have gone when the workers and the toilers used to suffer bitterly. We protect all of the them. And I am under the protection. All of us are under the protection of the people, we work for the people and derive strength from them.
items.sourceLine: Brothers! The days have gone when the workers and the toilers used to suffer bitterly. We protect all of the them. And I am under the protection. All of us are under the protection of the people, we work for the people and derive strength from them.

items.author: Abd al-Karim Qasim
items.quote: Brother workers! If you wish to stamp out imperialism, you have to exert yourself to work an extra hour. This will undermine the structure of the foreigner and the coloniser. An extra working hour can undermine the structure of the imperialists and threaten their existence.

items.quote: No longer shall the intrigues and mischief-making of the imperialists deceive us. No longer shall our work be interrupted under flimsy pretexts. We are working to attain a bright and better future, ensuring freedom and prosperous living not only to ourselves but to posterity.

items.author: Aṣa

items.sourceLine: We will not put an end to extreme poverty if we do not give priority to education especially, girls' education

items.author: Aṣa
items.quote: When you just can’t see the future, when you just can’t see the light, you always got to put on a fight.

items.author: Aṣa
items.quote: I know I can’t change the past, but as the river keeps flowing, I’ll keep on moving on.

items.author: Aṣa

items.sourceLine: “Universal quality education is one of the best antidotes to poverty”

items.author: Aṣa

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: Ah, my brave Arabs! If I could only gather them in from all their desert ways, and arm them properly… But I fear it cannot be. They are drifting in by tens and scores, where I need hundreds and thousands.
items.sourceLine: Ah, my brave Arabs! If I could only gather them in from all their desert ways, and arm them properly... But I fear it cannot be. They are drifting in by tens and scores, where I need hundreds and thousands.

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: We are taking care of our troops today, hence their loyalty. Formerly a rifle was given to a man and he had to shift for himself.
items.sourceLine: We are taking care of our troops today, hence their loyalty. Formerly a rifle was given to a man and he had to shift for himself.

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: All who seek to enrich those who do not work should be destroyed.
items.sourceLine: All who seek to enrich those who do not work should be destroyed.

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: The transformation of the Islamic world into one of revolution, as His Majesty has desired, had been in preparation for some time and had now been put into action.
items.sourceLine: The transformation of the Islamic world into one of revolution, as His Majesty has desired, had been in preparation for some time and had now been put into action.

items.quote: The threat could be eliminated by removing the Armenians from the places where they lived and sending them to other places.

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: If the Russians retreat, they are done.

items.author: İsmail Enver
items.quote: You are greatly mistaken. We have this country absolutely under our control. I have no desire to shift the blame onto our underlings and I am entirely willing to accept the responsibility myself for everything that has taken place.

items.quote: From 2000 and especially 2006 until today, and thanks also to social networks, my work has had a greater presence both in Mexico and internationally.
items.sourceLine: From 2000 and especially 2006 until today, and thanks also to social networks, my work has had a greater presence both in Mexico and internationally.

items.author: Ángel Boligán
items.quote: We are surrounded by absurd behavior, contradictions, manipulations and, just by looking around, I have dozens of ideas on how to make a drawing as a mirror and show the context.
items.sourceLine: We are surrounded by absurd behavior, contradictions, manipulations and, just by looking around, I have dozens of ideas on how to make a drawing as a mirror and show the context.

items.author: Ángel Boligán
items.quote: Thanks to globalization, new technologies and social networks, we know that what makes us laugh or saddens us, causes exactly the same reaction on the other side of the world.
items.sourceLine: Thanks to globalization, new technologies and social networks, we know that what makes us laugh or saddens us, causes exactly the same reaction on the other side of the world.

items.quote: The Charlie Hebdo case is disturbing for the entire guild. There are many taboos, intolerance and extremism. And our task is
items.sourceLine: The Charlie Hebdo case is disturbing for the entire guild. There are many taboos, intolerance and extremism. And our task is — to destroy them. I believe that clever and artistic, reasoned and convincing humor can push more and more walls in our world. And it can be done without insult or aggression.

items.author: Ángel Boligán
items.quote: I am inspired to create an illustrated chronicle of the world in which we live.
items.sourceLine: I am inspired to create an illustrated chronicle of the world in which we live.

items.author: Ángel Sixto Rossi
items.quote: We usually say that this is not Rosario, it's not Rosario yet. We are at a moment where it almost depends on us for this to not be Rosario, but if we are careless, it will be Rosario in three months, or it already is and it will be more blatant to see.

items.sourceLine: My wish it is that you should always provide the destitute with food.

items.quote: It is my considered opinion that in the fullness of time history will record the greatness of Michael Collins and it will be recorded at my expense.

items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: When Christianity was brought to her shores it was received with a joy and eagerness, and held with a tenacity of which there is hardly such another example.
items.sourceLine: When Christianity was brought to her shores it was received with a joy and eagerness, and held with a tenacity of which there is hardly such another example.

items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: Next to her services to religion, Ireland's greatest contribution to the welfare of humanity has been the example of devotion to freedom which she has given throughout seven hundred years.
items.sourceLine: Next to her services to religion, Ireland's greatest contribution to the welfare of humanity has been the example of devotion to freedom which she has given throughout seven hundred years.

items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: The Irish genius has always stressed spiritual and intellectual rather than material values.
items.sourceLine: The Irish genius has always stressed spiritual and intellectual rather than material values.

items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: No matter what the future may hold for the Irish nation, the seven years
items.sourceLine: No matter what the future may hold for the Irish nation, the seven years — 1916 to 1923 — must ever remain a period of absorbing interest. Not for over two hundred years has there been such a period of intense and sustained effort to regain the national sovereignty and independence. items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: Nature never intended me to be a partisan leader … Every instinct of mine would indicate that I was meant to be a dyed-in-the-wool Tory, or even a bishop, rather than the leader of a revolution.
items.sourceLine: Nature never intended me to be a partisan leader ... Every instinct of mine would indicate that I was meant to be a dyed-in-the-wool Tory, or even a bishop, rather than the leader of a revolution.

items.author: Éamon de Valera
items.quote: For Irishmen, there is no football game to match rugby and if all our young men played rugby not only would we beat England and Wales but France and the whole lot of them put together.
items.sourceLine: For Irishmen, there is no football game to match rugby and if all our young men played rugby not only would we beat England and Wales but France and the whole lot of them put together.

items.sourceLine: Of course I wrote most of the Constitution myself. I remember hesitating for a long time over the US presidential system. But it wouldn't have done — we were too trained in English democracy to sit down under a dictatorship which is what the American system really is.

items.author: Édouard Glissant
items.quote: For me, the arrival is the moment where all the components of humanity … consent to the idea that it is possible to be one and multiple at the same time; that you can be yourself and the other; that you can be the same and the different.

items.quote: What a pelisse! It's tawny brown with an old gold lining
items.sourceLine: What a pelisse! It's tawny brown with an old gold lining – staggering. It will make a wonderful background for some things I'm thinking of doing. Promise that when it's worn out you'll give it to me [Méry promised!].

items.author: Édouard Manet
items.quote: You can deduce everything about a woman from the way she holds her feet. Seductive women always turn their feet out. Don't expect to get anywhere with a woman who turns her feet in.
items.sourceLine: You can deduce everything about a woman from the way she holds her feet. Seductive women always turn their feet out. Don't expect to get anywhere with a woman who turns her feet in.

items.quote: I beg you, if I die, don't let me go piecemeal into the public collections, my work would not be fairly judged. I want to get in complete or not at all...Please, please, promise me one thing, never let my things go into a museum piecemeal.

items.quote: One must be of one's time and paint what one sees.

items.quote: Patience—with patience everything comes in due season.
items.sourceLine: Patience—with patience everything comes in due season.

items.author: Édouard René de Laboulaye
items.quote: Reputation is a jewel which nothing can replace; it is ten thousand times more valuable capital than your diamonds.
items.sourceLine: Reputation is a jewel which nothing can replace; it is ten thousand times more valuable capital than your diamonds.

items.quote: The desert is mute, and dead men tell no tales.

items.author: Édouard René de Laboulaye
items.quote: The first day a man is a guest, the second a burden, the third a pest.
items.sourceLine: The first day a man is a guest, the second a burden, the third a pest.

items.quote: Nothing is important save the spiritual state that enables one to subjectify one's thoughts to a sensation and to think only of the sensation, all the while searching to express it.

items.author: Éilís Ní Dhuibhne
items.quote: As a citizen, I often wonder what blind spot we have today. What abuse are we committing that the whole of society blindly condones? Cruelty to animals, as J. M. Coetzee might suggest? Environmental abuse? Road carnage? Indifference to the Third World?

items.author: Émile Augier
items.quote: L’amour chez les vieillards a d'étranges racines, Et trouve, comme un lierre aux fentes des ruines, Dans ces cœurs ravagés par le temps et les maux, Cent brèches où pousser ses tenaces rameaux.
items.sourceLine: L’amour chez les vieillards a d'étranges racines, Et trouve, comme un lierre aux fentes des ruines, Dans ces cœurs ravagés par le temps et les maux, Cent brèches où pousser ses tenaces rameaux.

items.author: Émile Augier
items.quote: La vérité sort mieux d’un tonneau que d'un puits.
items.sourceLine: La vérité sort mieux d’un tonneau que d'un puits.

items.author: Émile Augier
items.quote: La patrie est aux lieux où l’on a des amis.
items.sourceLine: La patrie est aux lieux où l’on a des amis.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: A people needs air, broad horizons, an ideal which charms its imagination and makes its heart beat; reduce it to household calculations, to the politics of party interests, it will disintegrate and corrupt itself.
items.sourceLine: A people needs air, broad horizons, an ideal which charms its imagination and makes its heart beat; reduce it to household calculations, to the politics of party interests, it will disintegrate and corrupt itself.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: The desert reveals its secrets; the great mystery of interior Africa is revealed day by day.
items.sourceLine: The desert reveals its secrets; the great mystery of interior Africa is revealed day by day.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: Everything seems to indicate that a decisive hour has sounded in the history of the world, the hour when an almost virgin continent and ignored races will cooperate in the work of humanity.
items.sourceLine: Everything seems to indicate that a decisive hour has sounded in the history of the world, the hour when an almost virgin continent and ignored races will cooperate in the work of humanity.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: Wherever this regime has been applied in one form or another, it has led to economic stagnation and decline and political revolt.
items.sourceLine: Wherever this regime has been applied in one form or another, it has led to economic stagnation and decline and political revolt.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: The King isolates himself and becomes less and less accessible to our advice.
items.sourceLine: The King isolates himself and becomes less and less accessible to our advice.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: You may want to, Sire, but then you will find someone other than me to carry out such a will.
items.sourceLine: You may want to, Sire, but then you will find someone other than me to carry out such a will.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: Belgium only does pure philanthropy.
items.sourceLine: Belgium only does pure philanthropy.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: The more we increase in numbers, the more we starve and become poorer. … Either our population will shrink, or our territory will expand.
items.sourceLine: The more we increase in numbers, the more we starve and become poorer. ... Either our population will shrink, or our territory will expand.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: The King is no longer the same; the change of character and spirit observed in him for two or three years is accentuated and makes fear of a catastrophe, at a time when he had only to let it go to be a remarkable King, perhaps to become a large figure.
items.sourceLine: The King is no longer the same; the change of character and spirit observed in him for two or three years is accentuated and makes fear of a catastrophe, at a time when he had only to let it go to be a remarkable King, perhaps to become a large figure.

items.author: Émile Banning
items.quote: It's my ruin you stipulate and you can't want it.
items.sourceLine: It's my ruin you stipulate and you can't want it.

items.author: Émile Borel
items.quote: Quels que soient les progrès des connaissances humaines, il y aura toujours place pour l'ignorance et par suite pour le hasard et la probabilité.
items.sourceLine: Quels que soient les progrès des connaissances humaines, il y aura toujours place pour l'ignorance et par suite pour le hasard et la probabilité.

items.author: Émile Boutroux
items.quote: He used to say that a philosophical system is a living thought; and, in truth, he not only taught his philosophy, but lived it, felt it, spread it and defended it in books and with words, in Europe and America, regardless of hardship, with all the ardour of a missionary.
items.sourceLine: He used to say that a philosophical system is a living thought; and, in truth, he not only taught his philosophy, but lived it, felt it, spread it and defended it in books and with words, in Europe and America, regardless of hardship, with all the ardour of a missionary.

items.author: Émile Bréhier
items.quote: Stoicism, which generally disappeared as the official School, was the most important of the Hellenistic elements in the semi-oriental religions of vanishing paganism.
items.sourceLine: Stoicism, which generally disappeared as the official School, was the most important of the Hellenistic elements in the semi-oriental religions of vanishing paganism.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: On prouve tout ce qu'on veut, et la vraie difficulté est de savoir ce qu'on veut prouver.
items.sourceLine: On prouve tout ce qu'on veut, et la vraie difficulté est de savoir ce qu'on veut prouver.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Thought is saying no, and it is to itself that thought says no.
items.sourceLine: Thought is saying no, and it is to itself that thought says no.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: When people ask me if the division between parties of the right and parties of the left, men of the right and men of the left, still makes sense, the first thing that comes to mind is that the person asking the question is certainly not a man of the left.
items.sourceLine: When people ask me if the division between parties of the right and parties of the left, men of the right and men of the left, still makes sense, the first thing that comes to mind is that the person asking the question is certainly not a man of the left.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Rien n’est plus dangereux qu’une idèe, quand on n’a qu’une idèe.
items.sourceLine: Rien n’est plus dangereux qu’une idèe, quand on n’a qu’une idèe.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: If religion is only human, and its form is man’s form, it follows that everything in religion is true.
items.sourceLine: If religion is only human, and its form is man’s form, it follows that everything in religion is true.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: It is the human condition to question one god after another, one appearance after another, or better, one apparition after another, always pursuing the truth of the imagination, which is not the same as the truth of appearance.
items.sourceLine: It is the human condition to question one god after another, one appearance after another, or better, one apparition after another, always pursuing the truth of the imagination, which is not the same as the truth of appearance.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: As opposed to the incoherent spectacle of the world, the real is what is expected, what is obtained and what is discovered by our own movement. It is what is sensed as being within our own power and always responsive to our action.
items.sourceLine: As opposed to the incoherent spectacle of the world, the real is what is expected, what is obtained and what is discovered by our own movement. It is what is sensed as being within our own power and always responsive to our action.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: It is clear that in mulling over harsh judgments, sinister predictions, and bad memories, we fashion our own sadness; in a certain sense, we savor it.
items.sourceLine: It is clear that in mulling over harsh judgments, sinister predictions, and bad memories, we fashion our own sadness; in a certain sense, we savor it.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: In short, the important thing is to get started. No matter how; then there will be time to ask yourself where you are going.
items.sourceLine: In short, the important thing is to get started. No matter how; then there will be time to ask yourself where you are going.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Our errors perish before we do. Let's not mummify them and keep them around.
items.sourceLine: Our errors perish before we do. Let's not mummify them and keep them around.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Everybody continually tries to get away with as much as he can; and society is a marvelous machine which allows decent people to be cruel without realizing it.
items.sourceLine: Everybody continually tries to get away with as much as he can; and society is a marvelous machine which allows decent people to be cruel without realizing it.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Any kind of barbarism, once established, will last.
items.sourceLine: Any kind of barbarism, once established, will last.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Idleness is the mother of all vices, but also of all virtues.
items.sourceLine: Idleness is the mother of all vices, but also of all virtues.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Work is the best and worst of all things; the best of it is voluntary, the worst of it is servile.
items.sourceLine: Work is the best and worst of all things; the best of it is voluntary, the worst of it is servile.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Every menial condition is bearable as long as one can exercise authority over one's work and be assured that the job is permanent.
items.sourceLine: Every menial condition is bearable as long as one can exercise authority over one's work and be assured that the job is permanent.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: We are advised and led along by second-rate moralists who only know how to work themselves into a delirium and pass their illness onto others.
items.sourceLine: We are advised and led along by second-rate moralists who only know how to work themselves into a delirium and pass their illness onto others.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: An author of antiquity said that every event has two handles, and that, in order to carry it, there is no sense in choosing the one that hurts the hand.
items.sourceLine: An author of antiquity said that every event has two handles, and that, in order to carry it, there is no sense in choosing the one that hurts the hand.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Certainly thinking is pleasant, but the pleasure of thinking must be subordinated to the art of making decisions.
items.sourceLine: Certainly thinking is pleasant, but the pleasure of thinking must be subordinated to the art of making decisions.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: Untie, liberate, and do not be afraid. He who is free is disarmed.
items.sourceLine: Untie, liberate, and do not be afraid. He who is free is disarmed.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: It is very true that we ought to think of the happiness of others; but it is not often enough said that the best thing we can do for those who love us is to be happy ourselves.
items.sourceLine: It is very true that we ought to think of the happiness of others; but it is not often enough said that the best thing we can do for those who love us is to be happy ourselves.

items.author: Émile Chartier
items.quote: When the pack is out hunting, the dogs do not fight among themselves.
items.sourceLine: When the pack is out hunting, the dogs do not fight among themselves.

items.author: Émile Coué
items.quote: Tous les jours, à tous points de vue, je vais de mieux en mieux.
items.sourceLine: Tous les jours, à tous points de vue, je vais de mieux en mieux.

items.author: Émile Coué
items.quote: When the imagination and willpower are in conflict, are antagonistic, it is always the imagination which wins, without any exception.
items.sourceLine: When the imagination and willpower are in conflict, are antagonistic, it is always the imagination which wins, without any exception.

items.author: Émile Coué
items.quote: You have in yourself the instrument of your cure.
items.sourceLine: You have in yourself the instrument of your cure.

items.author: Émile Coué
items.quote: Every day, in every way, I am getting better and better
items.sourceLine: People may wonder why I am content to prescribe such a general and apparently vague formula as "Every day, in every way, I am getting better and better" for all and every ailment. The reason is, strange as it may seem, that our subconscious mind does not need the details. The general suggestion that everything "in every way" is going well is quite sufficient to set up the procedure of persuasion which will carry its

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: At the age when the faculties droop, when stern experience has destroyed all sweet illusions, man may seek solitude; but, at twenty, the affections which he is compelled to repress are a tomb in which he buries himself alive.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: At the age when the faculties droop, when stern experience has destroyed all sweet illusions, man may seek solitude; but, at twenty, the affections which he is compelled to repress are a tomb in which he buries himself alive.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Instruction is to the proletary what liberty is to the slave: the latter emancipates the body, the former emancipates the intelligence.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Instruction is to the proletary what liberty is to the slave: the latter emancipates the body, the former emancipates the intelligence.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: The power of words is immense. A well-chosen word has often sufficed to stop a flying army, to change defeat into victory, and to save an empire.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: The power of words is immense. A well-chosen word has often sufficed to stop a flying army, to change defeat into victory, and to save an empire.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Whenever the good done to us does not touch and penetrate the heart, it wounds and irritates our vanity.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Whenever the good done to us does not touch and penetrate the heart, it wounds and irritates our vanity.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: No faith has triumphed without its martyrs.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: No faith has triumphed without its martyrs.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Illusions ruin all those whom they blind.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Illusions ruin all those whom they blind.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Utopia! such is the name with which ignorance, folly, and incredulity have always characterized the great conceptions, discoveries, enterprises, and ideas which have illustrated the ages, and marked eras in human progress.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Utopia! such is the name with which ignorance, folly, and incredulity have always characterized the great conceptions, discoveries, enterprises, and ideas which have illustrated the ages, and marked eras in human progress.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Modesty is the chastity of merit, the virginity of noble souls.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Modesty is the chastity of merit, the virginity of noble souls.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Servility is to devotion what hypocrisy is to virtue.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Servility is to devotion what hypocrisy is to virtue.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Without the ideal, this inexhaustible source of all progress, what would man be? and what would society be?
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Without the ideal, this inexhaustible source of all progress, what would man be? and what would society be?

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: There is more poverty in the human heart than misery in life.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: There is more poverty in the human heart than misery in life.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Which is the best religion? The most tolerant.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Which is the best religion? The most tolerant.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: The woman who loves us is only a woman, but the woman we love is a celestial being whose defects disappear under the prism through which we see her.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: The woman who loves us is only a woman, but the woman we love is a celestial being whose defects disappear under the prism through which we see her.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: A woman by whom we are loved is a vanity; a woman whom we love is a religion.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: A woman by whom we are loved is a vanity; a woman whom we love is a religion.

items.author: Émile de Girardin
items.quote: Esteem is the strongest of all sympathies.
items.section: A Thousand Flashes of French Wit, Wisdom, and Wickedness (1902)
items.sourceLine: Esteem is the strongest of all sympathies.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: There is no sociology worthy of the name which does not possess a historical character.
items.sourceLine: There is no sociology worthy of the name which does not possess a historical character.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Kant postulates God, since without this hypothesis morality is unintelligible. We postulate a society specifically distinct from individuals, since otherwise morality has no object and duty no roots.
items.sourceLine: Kant postulates God, since without this hypothesis morality is unintelligible. We postulate a society specifically distinct from individuals, since otherwise morality has no object and duty no roots.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: When mores are sufficient, laws are unnecessary. When mores are insufficient, laws are unenforceable.
items.sourceLine: When mores are sufficient, laws are unnecessary. When mores are insufficient, laws are unenforceable.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Solidarity can grow only in inverse ratio to personality.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: Solidarity can grow only in inverse ratio to personality.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Reality seems valueless by comparison with the dreams of fevered imaginations; reality is therefore abandoned.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: Reality seems valueless by comparison with the dreams of fevered imaginations; reality is therefore abandoned.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Solidarity which comes from likenesses is at its maximum when the collective conscience completely envelops our whole conscience and coincides in all points with it.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: Solidarity which comes from likenesses is at its maximum when the collective conscience completely envelops our whole conscience and coincides in all points with it.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: At the moment when this solidarity exercises its force, our personality vanishes, as our definition permits us to say, for we are no longer ourselves, but the collective life.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: At the moment when this solidarity exercises its force, our personality vanishes, as our definition permits us to say, for we are no longer ourselves, but the collective life.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Every society is a moral society. In certain respects, this character is even more pronounced in organised societies. Because the individual is not sufficient unto himself, it is from society that he receives everything necessary to him, as it is for society that he works.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: Every society is a moral society. In certain respects, this character is even more pronounced in organised societies. Because the individual is not sufficient unto himself, it is from society that he receives everything necessary to him, as it is for society that he works.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Methodological rules are for science what rules of law and custom are for conduct.
items.section: The Division of Labor in Society (1893)
items.sourceLine: Methodological rules are for science what rules of law and custom are for conduct.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: As an industrialist, I am free to apply the technical methods of former centuries; but by doing so, I should invite certain ruin.
items.sourceLine: As an industrialist, I am free to apply the technical methods of former centuries; but by doing so, I should invite certain ruin.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: Men already had ideas on law, morality, the family, the state, and society itself before the advent of social science, for these ideas were necessary conditions of his life
items.sourceLine: Men already had ideas on law, morality, the family, the state, and society itself before the advent of social science, for these ideas were necessary conditions of his life

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: When, then, the sociologist undertakes the investigation of some order of social facts, he must endeavour to consider them from an aspect that is independent of their individual manifestations.
items.sourceLine: When, then, the sociologist undertakes the investigation of some order of social facts, he must endeavour to consider them from an aspect that is independent of their individual manifestations.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: To pursue a goal which is by definition unattainable is too condemn oneself to a state of perpetual unhappiness.
items.sourceLine: To pursue a goal which is by definition unattainable is too condemn oneself to a state of perpetual unhappiness.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: It is society which, fashioning us in its image, fills us with religious, political, and moral beliefs that control our actions.
items.sourceLine: It is society which, fashioning us in its image, fills us with religious, political, and moral beliefs that control our actions.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: It is not human nature which can assign the variable limits necessary to our needs. They are thus unlimited so far as they depend on the individual alone. Irrespective of any external regulatory force, our capacity for feeling is in itself an insatiable and bottomless abyss.
items.sourceLine: It is not human nature which can assign the variable limits necessary to our needs. They are thus unlimited so far as they depend on the individual alone. Irrespective of any external regulatory force, our capacity for feeling is in itself an insatiable and bottomless abyss.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: A passion for the infinite is daily presented as a sign of moral distinction, when in fact it can only occur in disturbed minds which accord the status of a norm to the very disturbance from which they are suffering.
items.sourceLine: A passion for the infinite is daily presented as a sign of moral distinction, when in fact it can only occur in disturbed minds which accord the status of a norm to the very disturbance from which they are suffering.

items.author: Émile Durkheim
items.quote: The general conclusion of the book which the reader has before him is that religion is something eminently social.
items.section: The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life, 1912
items.sourceLine: The general conclusion of the book which the reader has before him is that religion is something eminently social.

items.author: Émile Gallé
items.quote: The aim of my work: The study of nature, the love of nature's art,and the need to express what one feels in one's heart.
items.sourceLine: The aim of my work: The study of nature, the love of nature's art,and the need to express what one feels in one's heart.

items.author: Émile Gallé
items.quote: The study of nature, the love of nature's art,and the need to express what one feels in one's heart.
items.sourceLine: The aim of my work: The study of nature, the love of nature's art,and the need to express what one feels in one's heart.

items.author: Émile Gallé
items.quote: Our roots are in the depths of the woods-on the banks of streams and among the mosses.
items.sourceLine: Our roots are in the depths of the woods-on the banks of streams and among the mosses.

items.author: Émile Lahoud
items.quote: That's why I'm saying you must have a quick ceasefire, because the more the Israelis escalate
items.sourceLine: That's why I'm saying you must have a quick ceasefire, because the more the Israelis escalate — the things they're doing now, it's not done in the 21st century, when they use smart bombs against civilian buildings, when they use phosphorus bombs and right now they're investigating about it, when they're throwing three tonne bombs on one building — well all this is not allowed. So what I'm saying, you should have a ce

items.author: Émile Lahoud
items.quote: The Israeli armed forces are destroying Lebanon, and the international community isn't trying to hold them back, but giving them more time to complete their plan of destruction.
items.sourceLine: The Israeli armed forces are destroying Lebanon, and the international community isn't trying to hold them back, but giving them more time to complete their plan of destruction.

items.author: Émile Legouis
items.quote: He became an optimist on the day when he perceived reality.
items.sourceLine: He became an optimist on the day when he perceived reality.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: There are two men inside the artist, the poet and the craftsman. One is born a poet. One becomes a craftsman.
items.sourceLine: There are two men inside the artist, the poet and the craftsman. One is born a poet. One becomes a craftsman.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: I am little concerned with beauty or perfection. I don't care for the great centuries. All I care about is life, struggle, intensity. I am at ease in my generation.
items.sourceLine: I am little concerned with beauty or perfection. I don't care for the great centuries. All I care about is life, struggle, intensity. I am at ease in my generation.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Paris flared — Paris, which the divine sun had sown with light, and where in glory waved the great future harvest of Truth and of Justice.
items.sourceLine: Paris flared — Paris, which the divine sun had sown with light, and where in glory waved the great future harvest of Truth and of Justice.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: If you shut up truth and bury it under the ground, it will but grow, and gather to itself such explosive power that the day it bursts through it will blow up everything in its way.
items.sourceLine: If you shut up truth and bury it under the ground, it will but grow, and gather to itself such explosive power that the day it bursts through it will blow up everything in its way.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: If you ask me what I came to do in this world, I, an artist, I will answer you: I am here to live out loud!
items.sourceLine: If you ask me what I came to do in this world, I, an artist, I will answer you: I am here to live out loud!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: The artist is nothing without the gift, but the gift is nothing without work.
items.sourceLine: The artist is nothing without the gift, but the gift is nothing without work.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Est-ce qu'une femme a besoin de savoir jouer et chanter? Ah! mon petit, tu es trop bête… Nana a autre chose, parbleu! et quelque chose qui remplace tout.
items.sourceLine: Est-ce qu'une femme a besoin de savoir jouer et chanter? Ah! mon petit, tu es trop bête... Nana a autre chose, parbleu! et quelque chose qui remplace tout.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Wasn't it true that the moment two women were together in the presence of their lovers their first idea was to do one another out of them? It was a law of nature!
items.sourceLine: Wasn't it true that the moment two women were together in the presence of their lovers their first idea was to do one another out of them? It was a law of nature!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Both women, looking different ways, kept shrugging their shoulders, and asking themselves how the deuce the other could tell such woppers!
items.sourceLine: Both women, looking different ways, kept shrugging their shoulders, and asking themselves how the deuce the other could tell such woppers!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Existence is so bitter for every one of us! Ought we not to forgive others much, my friend, if we wish to merit forgiveness ourselves?
items.sourceLine: Existence is so bitter for every one of us! Ought we not to forgive others much, my friend, if we wish to merit forgiveness ourselves?

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Those beasts have everything and we get nothing—not even a crust if we’re starving! The only thing they’re fit for is to be taken in! Just mark my words!
items.sourceLine: "Those beasts have everything and we get nothing—not even a crust if we’re starving! The only thing they’re fit for is to be taken in! Just mark my words!" Hortense and Berthe nodded, as though profoundly impressed by the wisdom of their mother’s pronouncements. She had long since convinced them of the absolute inferiority of men, whose sole function in life was to marry and to pay.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: You know, they’ll have their revenge." "Who will?" "The women, of course.
items.sourceLine: "You know, they’ll have their revenge." "Who will?" "The women, of course."

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Crever pour crever, je préfère crever de passion que de crever d'ennui!
items.sourceLine: Crever pour crever, je préfère crever de passion que de crever d'ennui!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: She wanted to live, and live fully, and to give life, she who loved life! What was the good of existing, if you couldn’t give yourself?
items.sourceLine: She wanted to live, and live fully, and to give life, she who loved life! What was the good of existing, if you couldn’t give yourself?

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Did not one spend the first half of one’s days in dreams of happiness and the second half in regrets and terrors?
items.sourceLine: Did not one spend the first half of one’s days in dreams of happiness and the second half in regrets and terrors?

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: If the world is to die of misery, at any rate let it die cheerfully, and in sympathy with itself!
items.sourceLine: If the world is to die of misery, at any rate let it die cheerfully, and in sympathy with itself!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Why had he found her unattractive? Now that she was all black and her face covered in a thin layer of coal-dust, she had a strange charm.
items.sourceLine: Why had he found her unattractive? Now that she was all black and her face covered in a thin layer of coal-dust, she had a strange charm.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: And, then, if only there were some truth in what the priests say, if only the poor of this world were rich in the next!
items.sourceLine: "And, then, if only there were some truth in what the priests say, if only the poor of this world were rich in the next!" These words were greeted with a burst of laughter, and even the children shrugged their shoulders, for the hard wind blowing from the outer world had taken away all their belief. They harbored a secret fear of ghosts down in the mine, but scoffed at the empty heavens.

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Oh, those bourgeois scum! One day they’d stuff 'em with champagne and truffles till their guts burst!
items.sourceLine: Oh, those bourgeois scum! One day they’d stuff 'em with champagne and truffles till their guts burst!

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: What was Art, after all, if not simply giving out what you have inside you? Didn’t it all boil down to sticking a female in front of you and painting her as you feel she is?
items.sourceLine: What was Art, after all, if not simply giving out what you have inside you? Didn’t it all boil down to sticking a female in front of you and painting her as you feel she is?

items.author: Émile Zola
items.quote: Oh, the fools, like a lot of good little schoolboys, scared to death of anything they’ve been taught is wrong!
items.sourceLine: Oh, the fools, like a lot of good little schoolboys, scared to death of anything they’ve been taught is wrong!

items.author: Éric de Moulins-Beaufort
items.quote: The Catholic Church is not the religious function of a given political society. It is a communion of an order quite different from what national belonging or the framework of the law can provide, a communion open to all.
items.sourceLine: The Catholic Church is not the religious function of a given political society. It is a communion of an order quite different from what national belonging or the framework of the law can provide, a communion open to all.

items.quote: Common wisdom holds that the most complicated thing in the universe (asides fom the universe itself) is the human brain. In actual fact, however, other objects are even more complex

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: I still can't go of course. But if I didn't go, I would disappoint a lot of people. One would consider it desertion. As betrayal. And that also counts in my decision-making. I will choose the moment myself. And it will be there soon.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: The question of who is allowed to stay on French soil is a political issue par excellence that should not be left to "an oligarchy of national and European judges. The French should be able to decide that for themselves.
items.sourceLine: The question of who is allowed to stay on French soil is a political issue par excellence that should not be left to "an oligarchy of national and European judges. The French should be able to decide that for themselves."

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: A French first name shows that you really want to belong. The family name refers to the civilization of the country of origin that is left behind. The French first name refers to the future.
items.sourceLine: A French first name shows that you really want to belong. The family name refers to the civilization of the country of origin that is left behind. The French first name refers to the future.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: For my ancestors, the arrival of the French was an enormous progress. The door to culture, freedom and emancipation opened, they were no longer second-class citizens.
items.sourceLine: For my ancestors, the arrival of the French was an enormous progress. The door to culture, freedom and emancipation opened, they were no longer second-class citizens.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: The brightest representatives of the Islamic diaspora have long figured out how to use this liberalism to blow up the remnants of the nation-state, free themselves from the weak authority of the republic, and establish the law of Allah in their own enclaves.
items.sourceLine: The brightest representatives of the Islamic diaspora have long figured out how to use this liberalism to blow up the remnants of the nation-state, free themselves from the weak authority of the republic, and establish the law of Allah in their own enclaves.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: Islam is a civilisation incompatible with the principles of France.
items.sourceLine: Islam is a civilisation incompatible with the principles of France.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: Thierry Baudet I met him once. A very likeable man. He wants the Netherlands to remain the Netherlands. Just as France has to remains France.
items.sourceLine: Thierry Baudet I met him once. A very likeable man. He wants the Netherlands to remain the Netherlands. Just as France has to remains France.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: The first problem is France's destination and demographics. The invasion of migration. We have a big problem and we absolutely have to solve it, otherwise France in 20 years will no longer be France, but an area like Lebanon with communities fighting each other.
items.sourceLine: The first problem is France's destination and demographics. The invasion of migration. We have a big problem and we absolutely have to solve it, otherwise France in 20 years will no longer be France, but an area like Lebanon with communities fighting each other.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: Trump has forged a coalition between the workers and the patriotic elite. I strongly believe in the coalition that has brought Trump together. Just like Boris Johnson. That, I think, is the political axis of the future.
items.sourceLine: Trump has forged a coalition between the workers and the patriotic elite. I strongly believe in the coalition that has brought Trump together. Just like Boris Johnson. That, I think, is the political axis of the future.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: I want France to be in Europe, but I want France to come before Europe… With me the European flag will never fly without the French Tricolor.
items.sourceLine: I want France to be in Europe, but I want France to come before Europe... With me the European flag will never fly without the French Tricolor.

items.author: Éric Zemmour
items.quote: Our commitment is that France will never come to resemble the abandoned Calais of today.
items.sourceLine: Our commitment is that France will never come to resemble the abandoned Calais of today.

items.author: Étienne Bonnot de Condillac
items.quote: The art of reasoning is nothing more than a language well arranged.
items.sourceLine: The art of reasoning is nothing more than a language well arranged.

items.author: Étienne Bonnot de Condillac
items.quote: We shall not … begin this logic by definitions, axioms, or principles; we shall begin by observing the lessons which nature gives us.
items.sourceLine: We shall not ... begin this logic by definitions, axioms, or principles; we shall begin by observing the lessons which nature gives us.

items.author: Étienne Bonnot de Condillac
items.quote: The tone in which an Englishman expresses anger would, in Italy, be only a mark of surprise.
items.sourceLine: The tone in which an Englishman expresses anger would, in Italy, be only a mark of surprise.

items.author: Étienne Bonnot de Condillac
items.quote: Our ideas are transformed sensations.
items.sourceLine: Our ideas are transformed sensations.

items.author: Étienne Bonnot de Condillac
items.quote: To the eye of God there are no numbers: seeing all things at one time, he counts nothing.
items.sourceLine: To the eye of God there are no numbers: seeing all things at one time, he counts nothing.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: Et de tant d'indignités que les bêtes elles-mêmes ne supporteraient pas si elles les sentaient, vous pourriez vous délivrer si vous essayiez, même pas de vous délivrer, seulement de le vouloir.
items.sourceLine: Et de tant d'indignités que les bêtes elles-mêmes ne supporteraient pas si elles les sentaient, vous pourriez vous délivrer si vous essayiez, même pas de vous délivrer, seulement de le vouloir.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: Soyez résolus à ne plus servir, et vous voilà libres. Je ne vous demande pas de le pousser, de l'ébranler, mais seulement de ne plus le soutenir, et vous le verrez, tel un grand colosse dont on a brisé la base, fondre sous son poids et se rompre.
items.sourceLine: Soyez résolus à ne plus servir, et vous voilà libres. Je ne vous demande pas de le pousser, de l'ébranler, mais seulement de ne plus le soutenir, et vous le verrez, tel un grand colosse dont on a brisé la base, fondre sous son poids et se rompre.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: There is in our souls some native seed of reason, which, if nourished by good counsel and training, flowers into virtue, but which, on the other hand, if unable to resist the vices surrounding it, is stifled and blighted.
items.sourceLine: There is in our souls some native seed of reason, which, if nourished by good counsel and training, flowers into virtue, but which, on the other hand, if unable to resist the vices surrounding it, is stifled and blighted.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: The good seed that nature plants in us is so slight and so slippery that it cannot withstand the least harm from wrong nourishment.
items.sourceLine: The good seed that nature plants in us is so slight and so slippery that it cannot withstand the least harm from wrong nourishment.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: The mob has always behaved in this way—eagerly open to bribes that cannot be honorably accepted, and dissolutely callous to degradation and insult that cannot be honorably endured.
items.sourceLine: The mob has always behaved in this way—eagerly open to bribes that cannot be honorably accepted, and dissolutely callous to degradation and insult that cannot be honorably endured.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: Ils veulent servir pour amasser des biens: comme s'ils pouvaient rien gagner qui fût à eux, puisqu'ils ne peuvent même pas dire qu'ils sont à eux-mêmes.
items.sourceLine: Ils veulent servir pour amasser des biens: comme s'ils pouvaient rien gagner qui fût à eux, puisqu'ils ne peuvent même pas dire qu'ils sont à eux-mêmes.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: Friendship … flourishes not so much by kindnesses as by sincerity.
items.sourceLine: Friendship ... flourishes not so much by kindnesses as by sincerity.

items.author: Étienne de La Boétie
items.quote: Friendship … receives its real sustenance from an equality that, to proceed without a limp, must have its two limbs equal.
items.sourceLine: Friendship ... receives its real sustenance from an equality that, to proceed without a limp, must have its two limbs equal.

items.sourceLine: Non dolet ipse Dolet, sed pia turba dolet.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Philosophy always buries its undertakers.
items.sourceLine: Philosophy always buries its undertakers.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: We can only choose between two kinds of life, the active and the contemplative.
items.section: Thomism: The Philosophy of Thomas Aquinas
items.sourceLine: We can only choose between two kinds of life, the active and the contemplative.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: The mathematician always proceeds from thought to being or things. Consequently, critical idealism was born the day Descartes decided that the mathematical method must henceforth be the method for metaphysics.
items.sourceLine: The mathematician always proceeds from thought to being or things. Consequently, critical idealism was born the day Descartes decided that the mathematical method must henceforth be the method for metaphysics.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Indeed, all idealism derives from Descartes, or from Kant, or from both together, and whatever other distinguishing features a system may have, it is idealist to the extent that, either in itself, or as far as we are concerned, it makes knowing the condition of being.
items.sourceLine: Indeed, all idealism derives from Descartes, or from Kant, or from both together, and whatever other distinguishing features a system may have, it is idealist to the extent that, either in itself, or as far as we are concerned, it makes knowing the condition of being.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: As used today, the word realism means in the first place the opposite to idealism when it claims that it is possible to pass from the subject to the object.
items.sourceLine: As used today, the word realism means in the first place the opposite to idealism when it claims that it is possible to pass from the subject to the object.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Reality can be grasped at levels of different depths. It is immediately given to us in a kind of block form, which is simply the "apprehended reality".
items.sourceLine: Reality can be grasped at levels of different depths. It is immediately given to us in a kind of block form, which is simply the "apprehended reality".

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: While Descartes finds being in thought, Saint Thomas finds thought in being.
items.sourceLine: While Descartes finds being in thought, Saint Thomas finds thought in being.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Up to Descartes' time, and particularly during the Middle Ages, it had always been agreed that philosophy consisted in a transposition of reality into conceptual terms
items.sourceLine: Up to Descartes' time, and particularly during the Middle Ages, it had always been agreed that philosophy consisted in a transposition of reality into conceptual terms

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Hume's skepticism, therefore, descends in a direct line from Cartesian mathematicism.
items.sourceLine: Hume's skepticism, therefore, descends in a direct line from Cartesian mathematicism.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: If there is a single initial error at the root of all the difficulties philosophy is involved in, it can only be the one Descartes committed when he decreed, a priori, that the method of one of the sciences of reality was valid for the whole of reality.
items.sourceLine: If there is a single initial error at the root of all the difficulties philosophy is involved in, it can only be the one Descartes committed when he decreed, a priori, that the method of one of the sciences of reality was valid for the whole of reality.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: The scientific sterility of the Middle Ages has to be condemned for the same reasons which make it necessary today to condemn the philosophic sterility of scientism.
items.sourceLine: The scientific sterility of the Middle Ages has to be condemned for the same reasons which make it necessary today to condemn the philosophic sterility of scientism.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: If there is something more in a living being than a pure mechanism, Descartes is bound in advance to miss it.
items.sourceLine: If there is something more in a living being than a pure mechanism, Descartes is bound in advance to miss it.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Most of our contemporaries think that, at bottom, being a philosopher and adopting an idealist method are one and the same thing.
items.sourceLine: Most of our contemporaries think that, at bottom, being a philosopher and adopting an idealist method are one and the same thing.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: Every given reality implies the thought which apprehends it. Therefore being is the condition of knowing; knowing is not the condition of being.
items.sourceLine: Every given reality implies the thought which apprehends it. Therefore being is the condition of knowing; knowing is not the condition of being.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: The realist method starts with the whole in order to distinguish the parts.
items.sourceLine: The realist method starts with the whole in order to distinguish the parts.

items.author: Étienne Gilson
items.quote: All realism derives from the analysis of knowledge; all idealism derives from the analysis of a thought.
items.sourceLine: All realism derives from the analysis of knowledge; all idealism derives from the analysis of a thought.

items.sourceLine: Only my faith and hope in that loving God who wants the good for all his sons enabled me to grow in spirit and strengthened me for the ups and downs of life. That is why I was able to succeed and I thank my Lord again and again.

items.quote: Why have accusations that were published and dismissed one year ago been published now, only 8 days before I present my resignation to Pope Francis, since I will have reached the age limit of 75? I will keep serving as long as the Holy Father wishes so.
items.sourceLine: Why have accusations that were published and dismissed one year ago been published now, only 8 days before I present my resignation to Pope Francis, since I will have reached the age limit of 75? I will keep serving as long as the Holy Father wishes so.

items.author: Óscar Vicente Ojea Quintana
items.quote: Life is the first right and without it no others can be given. We claim it for everyone at any age or in any situation that life finds itself in, and especially those who are weak, unprotected and defenseless
items.sourceLine: Life is the first right and without it no others can be given. We claim it for everyone at any age or in any situation that life finds itself in, and especially those who are weak, unprotected and defenseless

items.author: Ödön von Horváth
items.quote: Nichts gibt so sehr das Gefühl der Unendlichkeit als wie die Dummheit.
items.sourceLine: "Nichts gibt so sehr das Gefühl der Unendlichkeit als wie die Dummheit."

items.author: Ödön von Horváth
items.quote: Nothing conveys the feeling of infinity as much as stupidity does.
items.sourceLine: Translation: Nothing conveys the feeling of infinity as much as stupidity does.

items.author: Ömer Çelik
items.quote: We stand behind the resolutions of the UN Security Council and the UN General Assembly on Palestine
items.sourceLine: We stand behind the resolutions of the UN Security Council and the UN General Assembly on Palestine

items.author: Ömer Çelik
items.quote: Azerbaijan and Turkey are the two countries which have the same fate, same future and same values,
items.sourceLine: Azerbaijan and Turkey are the two countries which have the same fate, same future and same values,

items.author: Úrsula Corberó
items.quote: Well, it’s absolutely crazy. Before La Casa De Papel or Money Heist, the comments I always received were only in Spanish, of course. Now, some of them are even hard for me to understand because they’re in Arabic, Russian, you name it.
items.sourceLine: Well, it’s absolutely crazy. Before La Casa De Papel or Money Heist, the comments I always received were only in Spanish, of course. Now, some of them are even hard for me to understand because they’re in Arabic, Russian, you name it.

items.author: Úrsula Corberó
items.quote: I always look like a very confident person, and I think that I am, but that doesn't mean that I have no insecurities or fears. We all do! It's normal and it's good and we should normalise that.
items.sourceLine: I always look like a very confident person, and I think that I am, but that doesn't mean that I have no insecurities or fears. We all do! It's normal and it's good and we should normalise that.

items.author: Þórbergur Þórðarson
items.quote: My only wealth is philosophy. My only pride is wisdom.
items.sourceLine: My only wealth is philosophy. My only pride is wisdom.

items.author: Þórbergur Þórðarson
items.quote: The underlying tone of existence is harmless humour.
items.sourceLine: The underlying tone of existence is harmless humour.

items.author: Þórbergur Þórðarson
items.quote: But once people have had a huge glut of progress, they'll get bored. They'll start talking to the wind and flowers and stones again and listening to the song of the stars.
items.sourceLine: But once people have had a huge glut of progress, they'll get bored. They'll start talking to the wind and flowers and stones again and listening to the song of the stars.

items.author: Đorđe Balašević
items.quote: While we were growing up, the biggest insult for us was when dark emigrant forces called our homeland an unnatural, artificial creation. When we grew up, the biggest insult for us was when we realised that was true.
items.sourceLine: "While we were growing up, the biggest insult for us was when dark emigrant forces called our homeland an unnatural, artificial creation. When we grew up, the biggest insult for us was when we realised that was true."

items.author: Đorđe Balašević
items.quote: From far away, through the sights of a sniper, they would look like Muslims, Serbs or Croats to somebody, but I approached them face to face, I saw them clearly, and trust me… They were just people…
items.sourceLine: "From far away, through the sights of a sniper, they would look like Muslims, Serbs or Croats to somebody, but I approached them face to face, I saw them clearly, and trust me... They were just people..."

items.author: Đorđe Balašević
items.quote: Like Machiavelli would say, little Jovana was five months old, and I was prepared to write even
items.sourceLine: "Like Machiavelli would say, little Jovana was five months old, and I was prepared to write even "I saw Feldmarshall Göring three times", just to slip away from the barracks for two days and see my little girl and her beautiful mother."

items.author: Đặng Thị Ngọc Thịnh
items.quote: Women worldwide should unite for peace, friendly co-operation and development.
items.sourceLine: Women worldwide should unite for peace, friendly co-operation and development.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Thuở trời đất nổi cơn gió bụi, Khách má hồng nhiều nỗi truân chuyên. Xanh kia thăm thẳm tầng trên, Vì ai gây dựng cho nên nỗi này?
items.sourceLine: Thuở trời đất nổi cơn gió bụi, Khách má hồng nhiều nỗi truân chuyên. Xanh kia thăm thẳm tầng trên, Vì ai gây dựng cho nên nỗi này?

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Sứ trời sớm giục đường mây, Phép công là trọng, niềm tây sá nào.
items.sourceLine: Sứ trời sớm giục đường mây, Phép công là trọng, niềm tây sá nào.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Chàng tuổi trẻ vốn dòng hào kiệt, Xếp bút nghiên theo việc đao cung. Thành liền mong hiến bệ rồng, Thước gươm đã quyết chẳng dung giặc trời.
items.sourceLine: Chàng tuổi trẻ vốn dòng hào kiệt, Xếp bút nghiên theo việc đao cung. Thành liền mong hiến bệ rồng, Thước gươm đã quyết chẳng dung giặc trời.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Ðưa chàng lòng dằng dặc buồn, Bộ khôn bằng ngựa, thủy khôn bằng thuyền.
items.sourceLine: Ðưa chàng lòng dằng dặc buồn, Bộ khôn bằng ngựa, thủy khôn bằng thuyền.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Hà lương chia rẽ đường này, Bên đường, trông bóng cờ bay ngùi ngùi.
items.sourceLine: Hà lương chia rẽ đường này, Bên đường, trông bóng cờ bay ngùi ngùi.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Chàng thì đi cõi xa mưa gió, Thiếp thì về buồng cũ gối chăn.
items.sourceLine: Chàng thì đi cõi xa mưa gió, Thiếp thì về buồng cũ gối chăn.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Cùng trông lại mà cùng chẳng thấy, Thấy xanh xanh những mấy ngàn dâu. Ngàn dâu xanh ngắt một màu, Lòng chàng ý thiếp ai sầu hơn ai?
items.sourceLine: Cùng trông lại mà cùng chẳng thấy, Thấy xanh xanh những mấy ngàn dâu. Ngàn dâu xanh ngắt một màu, Lòng chàng ý thiếp ai sầu hơn ai?

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Hồn tử sĩ gió ù ù thổi, Mặt chinh phu trăng dõi dõi soi. Chinh phu tử sĩ mấy người, Nào ai mạc mặt, nào ai gọi hồn.
items.sourceLine: Hồn tử sĩ gió ù ù thổi, Mặt chinh phu trăng dõi dõi soi. Chinh phu tử sĩ mấy người, Nào ai mạc mặt, nào ai gọi hồn.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Những mong cá nước vui vầy, Ai ngờ đôi ngả nước mây cách vời.
items.sourceLine: Những mong cá nước vui vầy, Ai ngờ đôi ngả nước mây cách vời.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Thuở lâm hành oanh chưa mến liễu, Hỏi ngày về, ước nẻo quyên ca. Nay quyên đã giục, oanh già, Ý nhi lại gáy trước nhà líu lo.
items.sourceLine: Thuở lâm hành oanh chưa mến liễu, Hỏi ngày về, ước nẻo quyên ca. Nay quyên đã giục, oanh già, Ý nhi lại gáy trước nhà líu lo.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Lòng lão thân buồn khi tựa cửa, Miệng hài nhi chờ bữa mớm cơm. Ngọt bùi thiếp đã hiếu nam, Khuyến con đèn sách thiếp làm phụ thân.
items.sourceLine: Lòng lão thân buồn khi tựa cửa, Miệng hài nhi chờ bữa mớm cơm. Ngọt bùi thiếp đã hiếu nam, Khuyến con đèn sách thiếp làm phụ thân.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Bóng dương để hoa vàng chẳng đoái, Hoa để vàng vì tại bóng dương. Hoa vàng hoa rụng quanh tường, Trải xem hoa rụng đêm sương mấy lần.
items.sourceLine: Bóng dương để hoa vàng chẳng đoái, Hoa để vàng vì tại bóng dương. Hoa vàng hoa rụng quanh tường, Trải xem hoa rụng đêm sương mấy lần.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Thiếp xin chàng chớ bạc đầu, Thiếp thì giữ mãi lấy màu trẻ trung.
items.sourceLine: Thiếp xin chàng chớ bạc đầu, Thiếp thì giữ mãi lấy màu trẻ trung.

items.author: Đặng Trần Côn
items.quote: Lòng hứa quốc thắm son ngăn ngắt, Sức tý dân đụng sắt trơ trơ.
items.sourceLine: Lòng hứa quốc thắm son ngăn ngắt, Sức tý dân đụng sắt trơ trơ.

items.author: Łukasz Pawlikowski
items.quote: Sztuka nie pyta o wiek, tylko oczekuje wiele.
items.sourceLine: Sztuka nie pyta o wiek, tylko oczekuje wiele.

items.author: Łukasz Pawlikowski
items.quote: Kiedy miałem kilka lat, często podchodziłem do drzwi pokoju, w którym akurat ćwiczyła mama, wsłuchiwałem się w dźwięki i wyobrażałem sobie tę muzykę.
items.sourceLine: Kiedy miałem kilka lat, często podchodziłem do drzwi pokoju, w którym akurat ćwiczyła mama, wsłuchiwałem się w dźwięki i wyobrażałem sobie tę muzykę.

items.author: Ōnishi Aijirō
items.quote: それは、恐ろしい蔭の力を以て、弓き廻されるような感じで、不可抗力と言うべきで、甘露台様御自身、意識して行動せられたのでは無かったのである。宵から夜半まで無我夢中に歩き廻られて、突然、甘露台様が立ち止まられた。そして、座敷の中央へ出られた時、「此処は甘露台や」と思われた。

items.author: Ōnishi Tama
items.quote: 生も死も、借りしものにはなかりけり ただあるものは、神のおもわく sei mo shi mo, karishi mono ni wa nakarikeri tada aru mono wa, shin no o mo waku

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: With each loss, new buds of victory unfold in our hearts.
items.sourceLine: With each loss, new buds of victory unfold in our hearts.

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: So struggle! For struggle is life's flower; The fertile flower of life.
items.sourceLine: So struggle! For struggle is life's flower; The fertile flower of life.

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: I must cease the casting of my own chains. I must cease the binding of my body. I must break the chains that bind me. I must also create a new self, a new reality, a new sense of justice, a new fate.
items.sourceLine: I must cease the casting of my own chains. I must cease the binding of my body. I must break the chains that bind me. I must also create a new self, a new reality, a new sense of justice, a new fate.

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: The interaction of nothing with nothing—the relationship between nothing and nothing—will, ultimately, be nothing.
items.sourceLine: The interaction of nothing with nothing—the relationship between nothing and nothing—will, ultimately, be nothing.

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: Sloth has no ambition. Sloth makes no history.
items.sourceLine: Sloth has no ambition. Sloth makes no history.

items.author: Ōsugi Sakae
items.quote: Let freedom be for an idea, Let freedom be for an action, Still, let freedom be for a motive!
items.sourceLine: Let freedom be for an idea, Let freedom be for an action, Still, let freedom be for a motive!

items.author: Ōta Hakusetsu
items.quote: At peace,above my sicknesssummer smolders.
items.sourceLine: At peace,above my sicknesssummer smolders.

items.author: Śāriputra
items.quote: Venerable sir, this is the entire holy life (brahmacariya), that is, good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.
items.sourceLine: Venerable sir, this is the entire holy life (brahmacariya), that is, good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship.

items.quote: I do not seek for death, I do not seek for birth; I abide my time, when my time comes, I shall go.

items.author: Şihabetdin Märcani
items.quote: In religion three things do not exist but these things preserve it: national language, national dress and national customs.
items.sourceLine: In religion three things do not exist but these things preserve it: national language, national dress and national customs.

items.author: Želimir Puljić
items.quote: I am so shaken that I would rather be silent, pray to God and commiserate with people. I want to tell them that I am near.
items.sourceLine: I am so shaken that I would rather be silent, pray to God and commiserate with people. I want to tell them that I am near.

items.author: Željko Glasnović
items.quote: Laws are for nothing if there is no mechanism to implement them.
items.sourceLine: "Laws are for nothing if there is no mechanism to implement them."

items.author: Željko Glasnović
items.quote: Nobody has seen shovel here in the last ten years.
items.sourceLine: "Nobody has seen shovel here in the last ten years."
